intended_object: The standard dot product of ℚ^{n+1} restricted to the zero-sum hyperplane {x | Σ xᵢ = 0}, i.e. the bilinear form of the classical coordinate model of the root lattice Aₙ (from docstring and module doc).
explanation: The body restricts `dotProductBilin ℚ ℚ` to `singleParityCheckCode ℚ (Fin (n+1))`, which is defined as the kernel of the coordinate-sum map, i.e. the zero-sum hyperplane. `zeroSumForm_apply` (proved by rfl) confirms that it evaluates to the dot product of the underlying vectors. This is a specific object: the form of the Aₙ coordinate model, used to build `zeroSumLattice`. Working over ℚ with index set Fin (n+1) is what that model and the library's lattice framework require, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has only the building blocks (`dotProductBilin`, `BilinForm.restrict`), not this restricted form itself.
